reason: E1 directly supports the premise that nanoclustering at GBs reduces cohesion in the quinary alloy, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that reducing the number of elements decreases nanoclustering or SFE variability, nor that such changes improve ductility; these are extrapolations without cited support.
premises: Nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at grain boundaries reduces grain boundary cohesion in CrMnFeCoNi
Reducing the number of principal elements decreases the chemical driving force for nanocluster formation at grain boundaries
Local compositional fluctuations cause large variations in stacking fault energy in CrMnFeCoNi and CrCoNi
Reducing the number of elements moderates local compositional fluctuations and thus stacking fault energy variability
Enhanced grain boundary cohesion and more uniform stacking fault energy delay crack initiation and improve ductility
